claim_under_test.verdict: CONFIRMED EXACTLY for the population defined as build_run_assets.error LIKE 'frozen manifest validation failed:%' — 18 records, 18 distinct assets, 8 distinct runs. family_B_missing_manifest.what_it_is: NOT a registry-drift case. run.plan_manifest / plan_manifest_digest were NULL from the moment build_runs was inserted — validate_frozen_run_manifest's very first check ('missing frozen run manifest or digest', runner.py line ~244) fires immediately. Root cause (confirmed by reading the dispatch scripts, see code_paths.root_cause_family_B): a large family of one-off `platform/scripts/dispatch_*.py` scripts (e.g. dispatch_sampurti_a3_chart1_kshetra.py, dispatch_sampurti_p_g1_ka_kshetra_rebuild.py, dispatch_sampurti_a2prime_chart1_full.py) INSERT INTO build_runs directly with columns (chart_id, scope, scope_target, action, plan, state, triggered_by) and never populate plan_manifest/plan_manifest_digest at all — they predate or bypass the freeze mechanism that platform/src/app/api/cockpit/runs/route.ts computes. There is nothing to 're-freeze' for this family; the fix is making every build_runs-inserting code path go through the shared freeze helper (or reject manifest-less rows at claim time with a distinct, non-'frozen manifest' error name), which is a different, smaller fix than A3's stated scope.

registry_change_attribution.value: NOT ATTRIBUTABLE at the row-value level — asset_registry carries no history/audit table (checked: audit_log, audit_events, admin_audit_log all track unrelated things — LLM query audits and admin-on-profile actions, never asset_registry row changes; there is no asset_registry_history table and no trigger that logs old/new values on UPDATE, only `nirmana_registry_receipt_invalidation`, which invalidates a downstream receipt cache but discards the diff). What WOULD make this answerable: an append-only asset_registry_history table (or a `nirmana_invalidate_registry_receipts`-style trigger extended to also INSERT old/new row images) populated on every UPDATE of asset_registry, keyed by asset_id + changed_at, so a validation failure at time T could be joined back to 'which row(s) changed between freeze_time and T'.
circumstantial_findings: For BOTH real incidents (bg_yogas 2026-09-04, mi_kula 2026-09-06), the CURRENT (2026-09-26) live asset_registry row for the flagged asset matches the frozen manifest's captured values exactly on all 4 compared fields (scope, depends_on as a set, natural_key_partition, has_cowriters). Whatever value differed in the 24-second freeze-to-check window has since reverted/converged back to the original. This is strong evidence the divergence was TRANSIENT — concurrent write activity from another lane, not a deliberate, sticky change to that asset's own contract.

Neither bg_yogas (target_table=brahma_yoga_catalog) nor mi_kula (target_table=mimamsa_signal_families) has any peer sharing its target_table today — so has_cowriters is unambiguously false for both today, matching their frozen manifests. If has_cowriters was the field that flipped at validation time, the flip must have come from a THIRD asset (not bg_yogas/mi_kula itself, and not necessarily even in the run's plan) transiently gaining/losing is_active+has_writer on that same target_table.

git history around both incident windows shows an actively-running multi-lane autonomous swarm (L0-L5 'heartbeat' agents in 00_ARCHITECTURE/briefs/nirmana/sessions/) landing dozens of migrations per hour that touch asset_registry rows (depends_on fixes, e.g. 17102b048 'ka_muhurta_seva.depends_on corrects a fictional edge'; is_active/catalog_status changes as part of the 'asset_frozen' campaign lifecycle; integrity_check_sql rewrites, e.g. 0c3390ef3 'bg_yogas integrity_check_sql join-scope fix' merged 2026-09-06 00:58 UTC — after the 09-04 incident, so not itself the cause, but proof bg_yogas's registry row was under live, active editing in exactly this period). The mi_kula abort (09-06 17:23:59 UTC) falls inside a dense burst of same-minute registry-touching commits from the L0/L2/L4/L5 lanes.

A genuine, code-provable (not merely circumstantial) mechanism was found independent of these two incidents: freeze-time has_cowriters (route.ts) and check-time has_cowriters (runner.py) use ASYMMETRIC predicates over the same asset_registry table — see code_paths.sensitivity_finding. This alone can produce a false 'asset_registry changed' verdict with NO actual change to the flagged asset's own row, purely from a peer row's has_writer flag differing from what the (unfiltered-by-has_writer) freeze-time count assumed.
registry_change_attribution.conclusion_for_the_design_question: Both witnessed instances point AWAY from 'the change was related to the asset that failed.' bg_yogas's own row is, and (per the manifest snapshot) apparently was, unremarkable — the failure was triggered by registry-wide state (either a peer's is_active/has_writer flag, or the very fact that the freeze-time and check-time definitions of has_cowriters disagree) that has nothing to do with what bg_yogas or mi_kula themselves needed to build correctly. The premise behind A3 — 'an unrelated registry change is killing unrelated runs' — holds for family A. It does NOT explain family B, which is a wholly different bug (no manifest was ever attached).

freeze_point.function: POST handler, lines 368-412 (manifest assembly), manifestDigest() at line 97, canonicalManifestJson() at lines 83-94
freeze_point.what_it_captures_per_asset: asset_id, scope, depends_on (array, authored order), natural_key_partition, has_cowriters (boolean, DERIVED — see below), expected_code_digest (from a static writer-digest inventory JSON, not the DB) — plus run-level version/chart_id/scope/scope_target/action/waves.
freeze_point.has_cowriters_computation_at_freeze: lines 371-376: `writerCountByTarget` counts, over ALL rows returned by a query filtered only `WHERE is_active = true` (line 243), every row that HAS a target_table — has_writer is fetched (line 242) but NOT applied as a filter here. Then line 399: `has_cowriters: Boolean(entry.target_table && (writerCountByTarget.get(entry.target_table) ?? 0) > 1)`.
freeze_point.persisted_as: build_runs.plan_manifest (jsonb) + build_runs.plan_manifest_digest (sha256 hex), written by the INSERT at lines 571-576. A DB trigger (trg_build_runs_manifest_immutable, executing reject_build_run_manifest_mutation()) blocks any subsequent UPDATE of plan/plan_manifest/plan_manifest_digest — the manifest is immutable from the moment it lands, by DB constraint, not just by convention.

validation_point.entry: execute_run(), lines 1037-1040: `frozen = validate_frozen_run_manifest(run); _verify_registry_still_matches_manifest(cur, frozen); _verify_sidecar_code_matches_manifest(frozen)` — all three run BEFORE the wave-parallel scheduler starts, and before a single build_events row is emitted.
validation_point.validate_frozen_run_manifest: lines 234-325 — structural/self-consistency checks only (digest matches manifest, chart_id matches, waves flatten to plan, per-asset fields well-typed). Raises 'missing frozen run manifest or digest' at line ~244 if plan_manifest/plan_manifest_digest is NULL — this is family B's exact trigger.
validation_point.verify_registry_still_matches_manifest:
lines 343-374 — THE decisive comparison. Quoted in full:
```python
cur.execute(
    """SELECT ar.asset_id, ar.scope, COALESCE(ar.depends_on, '{}') AS depends_on,
              ar.natural_key_partition,
              EXISTS (
                SELECT 1 FROM asset_registry peer
                 WHERE peer.target_table = ar.target_table
                   AND ar.target_table IS NOT NULL
                   AND peer.asset_id <> ar.asset_id
                   AND peer.is_active = true AND peer.has_writer = true
              ) AS has_cowriters
       FROM asset_registry ar WHERE ar.asset_id = ANY(%s)""",
    (frozen.plan,),
)
rows = {row["asset_id"]: row for row in cur.fetchall()}
for asset_id in frozen.plan:
    row = rows.get(asset_id)
    if row is None:
        raise ValueError(f"frozen run manifest asset {asset_id} is no longer registered")
    if (
        row["scope"] != frozen.asset_scopes[asset_id]
        or sorted(row["depends_on"] or []) != sorted(frozen.asset_deps[asset_id])
        or row.get("natural_key_partition") != frozen.asset_partitions[asset_id]
        or bool(row.get("has_cowriters")) != frozen.asset_has_cowriters[asset_id]
    ):
        raise ValueError(f"asset_registry changed after dispatch for frozen asset {asset_id}")
```
The loop iterates `frozen.plan` IN ORDER and raises on the FIRST mismatching asset_id — it does not check, and therefore cannot report, whether any OTHER asset in the plan also diverged; the exception carries only the one name.
validation_point.abort_propagation: the ValueError from ANY of the three validators is caught once, at the top of execute_run (lines 1041-1048), and handled identically regardless of which asset (if any) was named: `_terminalize_preflight_failure(cur, run_id=run_id, message=message[:2000])` (defined lines 326-341) runs one SQL statement that (a) sets build_runs.state='failed' and (b) sets EVERY build_run_assets row for that run_id with state='queued' to state='aborted', stamping the SAME message text onto all of them. There is no per-asset granularity anywhere in this path: the run-level exception is translated directly into an all-rows UPDATE. This is why every one of the 8 observed runs shows 100% blast radius regardless of plan size (1 asset or 10).

root_cause_family_B.file_pattern: platform/scripts/dispatch_sampurti_*.py, dispatch_d*.py, dispatch_utkarsha_*.py, rebuild_*.py (dozens of one-off campaign scripts)
root_cause_family_B.finding: these scripts INSERT INTO build_runs (chart_id, scope, scope_target, action, plan, state, triggered_by) VALUES (...) — plan_manifest and plan_manifest_digest are simply absent from the column list, defaulting to NULL (the table's own CHECK constraint `build_runs_plan_manifest_pair_check` only requires the pair be NULL-or-non-NULL together, so this is a legal insert). These scripts predate/bypass the freeze mechanism that only platform/src/app/api/cockpit/runs/route.ts implements. Every one of family B's 6 runs is this pattern.

sensitivity_finding.claim: the manifest is NOT sensitive to timestamps, updated_at, row counts, or display fields — the 4 compared fields (scope, depends_on, natural_key_partition, has_cowriters) are all structurally load-bearing for build correctness (DAG scope/ordering/idempotency-key scoping). That part of the design is sound and should NOT be loosened.
sensitivity_finding.but: has_cowriters is not a column on the asset's own row — it is DERIVED via an EXISTS-peer-lookup across the ENTIRE asset_registry table, evaluated once at freeze time (route.ts) and re-evaluated fresh at validation time (runner.py) with a DIFFERENT filter predicate:

asymmetry.freeze_time (route.ts:371-376, 399): counts peers among rows already filtered `WHERE is_active = true` (route.ts:243) with a `target_table` set — has_writer is fetched but NEVER applied as a filter in this count.
asymmetry.check_time (runner.py:348-354): requires the peer to satisfy `peer.is_active = true AND peer.has_writer = true`.

sensitivity_finding.consequence: has_cowriters can be computed as true at freeze time (an is_active, has_writer=false reference/placeholder row shares the target_table) and false at check time (that same row still has has_writer=false, correctly excluded by the check-time predicate) — or vice-versa if a row's has_writer flips between freeze and check — producing a false 'asset_registry changed' verdict for an asset whose OWN scope/depends_on/natural_key_partition never moved, and whose actual co-writer situation never meaningfully changed either. This is sensitivity the check does not need: has_cowriters should be computed with the IDENTICAL predicate in both places (pick one: always require has_writer=true, since that is what actually matters for a shared-table write hazard).

recommendation.value: SPLIT the fix; do not treat the 18/8 figure as one problem.
recommendation.for_family_A_asset_registry_changed_11_r: FAIL ONLY GENUINELY-AFFECTED ASSETS, not 're-freeze and continue'. Evidence: (1) the check already computes a full per-asset row (scope/depends_on/natural_key_partition/has_cowriters) for every asset in frozen.plan in ONE query (runner.py:345-357) — the data to identify exactly which asset(s) diverged already exists in `rows`; the code just throws it away and stops at the first mismatch instead of collecting all mismatches. Re-scoping the abort to only the diverging asset(s) plus their downstream dependents (mirroring the existing _mark_asset_blocked cascade machinery already used elsewhere in this file for dependency-not-lit blocking) is a mechanical, low-risk change against code that's already shaped for it. (2) 'Re-freeze and continue' means silently accepting a live registry mutation mid-run and treating it as the new ground truth — that defeats the actual safety purpose of freezing (a genuine, sticky scope/depends_on change to an asset SHOULD block that asset, because the wave/DAG ordering computed at freeze time may no longer be valid for it). Re-freezing cannot distinguish a benign transient (what both witnessed incidents actually were) from a real incompatibility without re-running the planner, which is a much larger, riskier change than narrowing the blast radius of an abort that's already correct in WHICH asset it names. (3) Independently of the blast-radius question, fix the has_cowriters freeze/check predicate asymmetry (code_paths.sensitivity_finding) — this is a provable false-positive source and costs nothing to align (make route.ts's writerCountByTarget honor has_writer the same way runner.py's EXISTS clause does).
recommendation.for_family_B_missing_manifest_7_records_: Different bug, different fix, out of A3's stated scope as written: make every build_runs-inserting path (the dozens of one-off platform/scripts/dispatch_*.py scripts) go through the same freeze helper route.ts uses, or centralize freeze-computation into a shared library both the route and the scripts call. There is no 'registry changed' to react to here — the manifest was simply never created. Recommend flagging this to whoever owns A3's scope before implementation starts, since 6 of the 8 'runs' in the headline figure are this unrelated defect.
recommendation.what_not_to_change: the SET of compared fields (scope, depends_on, natural_key_partition, has_cowriters) is well-chosen and structurally load-bearing — do not loosen it to fix a blast-radius/asymmetry problem that has a narrower, more targeted fix available.
